answer: A reputation bridge between an agent's past work and its future access stops cheap fake identities: new agents start in a shallow lagoon of low-value tasks, earning trust only through verified deliveries. Each success raises their stake and their exposure, so creating many fake identities multiplies the work an attacker must do instead of dividing it. A sybil spiral forms — fakes burn time and fees on low-paying work while honest agents climb — making identity forgery cost more than it can ever earn back.
